headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: Replit Agent can write/browse broad Repl workspaces while pdf.js reads PDFs, creating shared-workspace exposure and unsafe downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A shared workspace is plausible because pdf.js reads PDF files and Replit Agent reads/writes Repl workspace files. If pdf content is later copied into the agent workflow, malicious instructions embedded in a PDF could influence Replit Agent. No direct automatic channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Replit Agent prompts or files
IF a PDF contains instruction-like text that Replit Agent treats as trusted
mitigations: Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate folder from Replit workspaces
Manually inspect PDFs before passing text to Replit Agent
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores instructions inside documents
Add a human review step before any agent action
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to document-derived text

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js handles PDF documents, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress. If PDF content includes sensitive material and is moved into the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can expose it through networked actions or logs. The shared-file path is enough to make leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive PDF content is copied into the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent is allowed to transmit workspace contents to external services or deployments
mitigations: Do not place sensitive PDFs in the Repl workspace
Redact secrets before any PDF-to-Repl transfer
Disable external deployment or API calls during document handling
Review generated files for leaked text before saving
requires-engineering: isolate document-processing and coding workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js can process PDF files and Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl filesystem. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent edits can overwrite artifacts or corrupt git state. The overlap is explicit in the profiles, so the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl filesystem path
IF Replit Agent modifies git state while pdf.js writes or rewrites files
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or snapshot before running the second agent
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repository
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js produces document-processing outputs that Replit Agent could use as inputs when building code or configs. Because Replit Agent has action-taking authority, any unverified extraction from pdf.js can cascade into incorrect edits or deployments. The profiles do not show an explicit verification gate, so the default risk is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes pdf.js-extracted text as authoritative
IF the extracted text contains incorrect or stale facts used in code or deployment changes
mitigations: Require manual verification of extracted facts
Compare extracted text against the original PDF
Limit Replit Agent to drafting, not executing, changes
Use a checklist before any deployment step
requires-engineering: add structured validation between extraction and action

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF documents, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl environment with broad egress. If regulated or sensitive PDFs are moved into Replit, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles show no documented compliance controls or DPA-like safeguards, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF PDFs contain regulated personal data or secrets
IF those PDFs are stored or processed inside a Replit workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of Replit
Strip identifiers before upload
Use a local-only document processor for sensitive files
Review retention settings for any copied artifacts
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls
